title: Factory overview: what is in flight, waiting, delivered and failing, per repo and fleet-wide

story.i_want_to: see per repo and for the whole fleet what is moving, what is waiting and why things fail
story.so_that: I can choose where to look and intervene, without anything turning red to get my attention

rationale: PRD R4: 'per repo and fleet-wide: what is in flight, what is waiting, throughput and failure classes'. Nothing aggregates the delivery stage machine today: GET /projects/:id/progress (project_controller.ex:717) counts stories by agent_status, which is the claim's status and says nothing about stages, escalations or throughput; GET /escalations (EscalationInbox.list/2, escalation_inbox.ex:237) lists escalated rows one by one. This story adds the one aggregate read fleet_dash polls, built on story_stages and the event log.

acceptance_criteria.description: Loopctl.Delivery.Overview.for_tenant/2 (tenant_id, opts) returns %{projects: [row], fleet: totals} with one row per active project of the tenant that has a live intake source or a story_stages row, each naming project_id, slug and repo_key; fleet is the sum of the rows.
Each row's in_flight is a count per stage for claimed, worktree, implementing, reviewing, pr_open, ci, merged, deployed and verified, read from story_stages.

Each row's waiting holds counts for detected, triaged and queued, and escalated counted per EscalationInbox.reason_class/1 of the edge each item entered escalated over, each with the age in seconds of its oldest item.

Each row's throughput holds, over a window of window_days (default 7, allowed 1..30), the count of transitions into done and the median seconds from an item's 'opened' event to its transition into done.
Each row's failure_classes counts, over the same window, the transitions into escalated and into failed grouped by edge, so a class is named by the machine's own edge and never by reason text.

GET /api/v1/factory/overview (role: :agent) takes optional project_id and window_days; window_days outside 1..30 or a non-integer is 400 naming the range; a project_id of another tenant or unknown is 404; another tenant's stories never appear in any count.

MCP tool factory_overview calls the route with project_id and window_days, has a mcp-server/README.md row and a wiring test; its description says the counts are read from the stage machine and that drill-down is work_item_timeline.

A migration adds index story_stage_events_tenant_to_stage_inserted_idx on (tenant_id, to_stage, inserted_at) WHERE event = 'transitioned', CONCURRENTLY, and the window queries of AC-52.30.4 and AC-52.30.5 use it (EXPLAIN in the test shows an index scan on a seeded table).

test_cases.name: rows per project and fleet totals, stage counts (DataCase)
preconditions: tenant with projects chg and hcb, each with an intake source fixture; stage rows at claimed, ci and merged in chg, implementing in hcb; an archived project with stage rows
expected_results: two rows, the archived project absent; fleet in_flight sums both

test_cases.name: waiting counts by reason class with oldest age (DataCase)
preconditions: escalated rows entered over :attempts_exhausted, :merge_gate and :triage_escalate at known times; two queued rows
expected_results: session_failed 1, gate_refused 1, triage_escalated 1, each with its age; queued 2

test_cases.name: throughput and failure classes inside the window only (DataCase)
preconditions: three items reaching done 2, 5 and 9 days ago; one :merge_gate escalation 3 days ago; one :triage_reject 10 days ago
expected_results: done 2 with their median; failure_classes %{merge_gate: 1}, triage_reject outside the window

test_cases.name: route parameters, roles and tenant isolation (ConnCase)
preconditions: a holder agent key and a user key in tenant A; a project in tenant B

test_cases.name: factory_overview wiring and request shape (node --test)
preconditions: mcp-server tool list and a stub apiCall

test_cases.name: window queries use the transition index (DataCase)
preconditions: 5,000 seeded transitioned events across stages; ANALYZE story_stage_events
steps: EXPLAIN the throughput query Overview builds

technical_notes: Stage counts: story_stages has index (tenant_id, stage) (priv/repo/migrations/20260915120000_create_story_stages.exs:62); the overview names its own sets, because neither StageMachine helper is one of them: in_flight is StageMachine.in_flight_stages/0 (claimed through ci, lib/loopctl/delivery/stage_machine.ex:642, the stages a runner holds) plus merged, deployed and verified, which that helper leaves out on purpose (:169-172); waiting is detected, triaged, queued and escalated, while terminal_stages/0 (:646) counts escalated as terminal. A test asserts that every stage of StageMachine.stages/0 (:634) falls in exactly one of in_flight, waiting, done and failed, so a stage added to the machine fails it until the overview places it.

Reason classes: EscalationInbox.reason_class/1 (lib/loopctl/delivery/escalation_inbox.ex:185) over the edge of the newest 'transitioned' event into escalated, the same read EscalationInbox uses; the escalation inbox route GET /escalations (router.ex:478) stays as the per-item drill-down.
Project rows: Projects with status active joined to Intake.live_sources_query/1 (lib/loopctl/intake.ex:1293) or to story_stages through stories.project_id; repo_key is provided by US-52.1.

Why not extend GET /projects/:id/progress: Projects.get_project_progress/2 (project_controller.ex:720) is a per-project count of stories.agent_status read by existing clients; stage aggregates are a different fact, and the overview is fleet-wide, which a project-scoped route cannot be.

Every query runs on Repo inside Repo.with_tenant/2 with an explicit tenant_id predicate, one aggregate query per section, under a statement_timeout of 5 s; a timeout is 503 busy, never a partial answer.
Migration: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY needs @disable_ddl_transaction and @disable_migration_lock; name it after git fetch origin (README Lanes rule 3).
MCP: lib/factory.js with the request shape, declaration and case in mcp-server/index.js, README row, wiring test.
non_goals: Whether a project's intake is paused: US-52.33 adds it to this read.
Alerts, colours or thresholds: nothing in the overview draws attention (PRD R4).

failure_modes.partition: n/a: aggregate reads inside one request against loopctl's own Postgres; no other service.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.30.2: every count is derived from story_stages and the event log at read time; the overview stores nothing, so a restart or deploy loses nothing and nothing can drift.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.30.6: a GET with no side effect, so a retried read is harmless.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.30.8: window queries run on a partial index and under a 5 s statement timeout (technical_notes), so a large tenant degrades to a 503 rather than holding a connection.
failure_modes.reach: n/a: runs inline in the request process; nothing is queued.

definition_of_done: factory_overview from an MCP session on production returns one row for each of chg, loopctl and home_care_billing with non-negative counts, and fleet equals their sum.
EXPLAIN on production for the throughput query shows the new index.
defaults: Median, not mean, for detected-to-done time.
Statement timeout for the overview queries: 5 s.
